phase-summary.outcome: Schema-authored JSON now generates the runtime codec/code-asset layer, Escape the Dungeon runtime boundaries decode typed bundles instead of leaning on handwritten duplicate contract surfaces, and the docs-site compatibility layer no longer compiles a second shadow engine runtime.

changes.change: Added authored bundle/source schemas plus `generate-contract-codecs.mjs` so TypeScript, C++, and C# codec/code-asset outputs are generated from repo JSON Schema.
Replaced the handwritten engine contract entrypoint with a thin wrapper around generated quicktype models and decode helpers.
Collapsed `docs-site/lib/escape-the-dungeon` from a duplicate runtime tree to a compatibility shim surface and removed the stale local contract mirror/data files.
Updated Kaplay and Space Explorer bundle loading paths to consume decoded `ContentPackBundle` data and keep loose typing only at local snapshot/editor-storage boundaries.
Updated release-artifact generation to emit the generated codec outputs alongside manifest/schema artifacts.
Fixed the final docs-site type boundary mismatches by storing active-pack snapshots as `unknown`, narrowing on read, and removing dead shim re-exports that were not consumed anywhere.

requriements-suggestions.item: Follow-on work should formalize the docs-site report/build-route payloads as schema-backed transport contracts so report/session snapshots do not rely on ad hoc partial objects.

Future Unreal work should consume the generated C++ outputs through an editor/importer pipeline that materializes `.uasset` content inside Unreal rather than attempting binary asset generation in Node.
